positions.name: CalibrationVerifiedAgainstReferenceStandard
positions.frame: What establishes the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration as verified — the appeal to the June reference plates as governing standard, or the assertion of the reading itself?
positions.why: All three expressions state the same calibration fact — instrument, frequency, verification basis — but in different registers: src-1 is Quill Ashgrove's prose claim performing the verification act ('verified the calibration against the June reference plates'), while src-2 and src-3 are Xena's structured field-labels restating the same content in flat technical shorthand (register mint-1: FlatTechnicalLogbook). Across all three the directional read is consistent — authority-ranking deference to the reference plates as the arbiter (relational, src-1/src-3), competence as the appealed-to good (value), unhedged claim-level conviction, and expert/informational power grounded in a demonstrated procedure rather than assertion alone. The tension held here is between the narrated act of verification (src-1) and the bare structured record of its outcome (src-2, src-3) — the group reads both as expressions of the same underlying grounding move, without resolving which carries more weight.

placements.why: This envelope's entire content is an observatory instrument calibration record (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates) submitted as a discrete organizational activity in its own right — nothing in the empty existing strata comes close to an instrument-calibration category, and the perspective's own focus framing ('observatory instrument calibration decisions') signals this is a standing organizational category future calibration envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. Minting it standalone since nothing existing is even adjacent.

placements.why: All three expressions carry the same recurring thematic content, in different registers: src-1 is Quill Ashgrove's prose narration of verifying the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration against June reference plates and confirming it holds across the observing band; src-2 and src-3 are Xena's structured field-labels restating the identical grounding move in flat technical shorthand. The specific numbers (88.4 MHz, June plates) are the evidence, not the leaf — the theme that persists beyond these words is that calibration is established by appeal to a governing reference standard, a subject future calibration envelopes for other instruments will keep feeding. No existing narrative leaf exists yet (structure was empty), so minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
